## Frozen additive contracts

1. In sim/types, export `NoticeChannel = "action" | "hazard" | "system" | "persistence"`, `NoticeContext = "threat" | "oxygen" | "food" | "hull" | "recovery"`, and `NoticeOptions { channel?: NoticeChannel; context?: NoticeContext }`. Add these optional fields to the existing notice event, preserving message/error. No saved fields or notice text changes. Tag step command results/refusals as action; survival notices as hazard with their actual context; threat notices as hazard/threat. Tag automatic recovery results at their step composition boundary without editing recovery.ts; use action/recovery for ordinary progress and hazard/recovery for errors. `error` alone is never a category classifier. An action refusal must not masquerade as a persistence failure. No new notice queue or UI behavior in this batch.
2. Extend `SessionEvents.notify(message, error?, options?: NoticeOptions)` compatibly. Tag actual disk/save/import-write failures and session-only/unsaved reminders persistence; successful save/import/new acknowledgements persistence too, with error false. Cancellation, migration and invalid/unreadable import-file messages are system (preserve error values). Current two-argument callbacks remain valid and may ignore the metadata until integration. Preserve every current writer, commit, cancel/generation, protected-slot, fallback-choice and entered/changed ordering. Do not introduce new asynchronous work, notifications or string classification.
3. Add optional `source?: "threat-call"` to sound events. Mark only the existing positional warning calls emitted on warn/pursue transitions; retain copied origin, cue, emission order and all timings. A later direction cue may retain the emitted sound location briefly; this metadata must not grant continuous omniscient tracking. Damage/body/equipment sounds remain unchanged. Existing state supplies threat transitions; no extra saved timer or new repeated call.
4. Add read-only `airSupply(s)` in survival.ts, returning `{ kind: "craft" | "refuge" | "surface" | "emergency" | "suit"; remainingSeconds: number | null }`. Share the existing suit drain rate with updateSurvival through an exported `SUIT_OXYGEN_DRAIN_PER_SECOND = 100 / 180`; preserve arithmetic/rates. Healthy powered controlled craft takes precedence, then actual refuge, then surface airway, then a controlled craft's positive emergency reserve, then suit oxygen divided by the same drain. Continuous air has null seconds; emergency reports only that reserve, suit only its actual remaining oxygen. Healthy craft cannot be relabelled generic refuge. A powerless craft at a genuinely breathable surface/refuge still has external air even while its existing emergency timer drains. Derive from existing exposure/controlled craft; do not broaden refuge/air rules or reset reserves. Leave exposure's existing return shape intact for consumers.
5. Add transient `ascent-sample` to GameEvent with fields `actorId: string | null`, `requestedRise: number`, `actualRise: number`, `solidLimitedRise: number`, `surfaceLimitedRise: number` (metres for this fixed step). Emit at most once per step, only for an actively commanded positive upward swim or piloted submerged-craft attempt with positive intended rise. No sample for walking/interiors/opening, passive inertia without upward intent, station-kept/disabled/unpowered craft, or the deliberately surface-only Spindle. Absence is the later app's reset signal. Measure against the **actual existing move results** before deliberate surface clamping: aggregate any positive requested-versus-achieved Y loss caused by `hitSolid`, and separately loss from the existing surface cap. Preserve net final actualRise, including a legitimate negative slide. Do not equate a side collision with blocked ascent when Y travel succeeds; do not count floor support correction, boundary clamp, or the surface cap as a ceiling. Use current slice/velocity computations without changing their order or values. Exclude sample if a subsequent same-step mode/actor replacement or incapacity makes it stale. A later app-owned accumulator decides whether the physical shortfall persists long enough for a cue; no WeakMap, hidden sim history, saved timer or global cache.

If a named contract cannot reflect the real current flow without a behavior change, report the exact evidence and proposed amendment while continuing other owned work. Do not silently change movement/survival to satisfy a presentation measurement.
